matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the numeric gap between the two sides before attempting any stick moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after reading the puzzle, to know how much the left and right sides differ.
matchstick.example: Skipping the conversion step and moving a stick arbitrarily, which can leave the equation still false.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Generate every way a single matchstick can be removed from one character and added to another (or repositioned within the same character), while keeping all characters valid Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After knowing the numeric discrepancy, to create a complete set of candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Considering a move that would leave a character with an invalid shape, such as removing one diagonal from X and ending up with a lone diagonal line.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, compute how the values of the affected numerals change and keep only those moves whose net change equals the required numeric discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating each enumerated transformation to filter out ineffective moves.
matchstick.example: Choosing a transformation that changes a numeral by +2 when the equation is off by +5, resulting in a still‑incorrect equality.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A ‘+’ consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into ‘-’, and removing the horizontal stick turns it into ‘I’. Adding a missing stick can reverse these changes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy suggests that changing an addition to subtraction (or creating an extra I) could resolve the equation.
matchstick.example: Turning ‘+’ into ‘-’ without adjusting the surrounding numbers, which can produce a negative result that cannot be expressed in Roman numerals.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If moving a stick from an operator to a numeral yields exactly the needed value change, relocate the stick and adjust the operator accordingly (e.g., ‘+’ → ‘-’, ‘=’ → ‘-’).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the required numeric adjustment can be achieved by converting an operator into a different operator or numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from ‘=’ to a numeral but leaving ‘=’ with only one horizontal line, which is no longer a valid equality sign.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one ‘=’, at least one valid numeral on each side, and only allowed operators (+, -).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate transformation, before accepting it as a solution.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from ‘=’ and turning it into ‘-’, resulting in an equation without an equality sign.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Use a lookup of common one‑stick numeral changes (e.g., I→II (+1), I→IV (+3), V↔X (+5), I↔V (+4)) to quickly assess the value impact of a move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When matching the numeric discrepancy to a known transformation.
matchstick.example: Attempting to change X to V by removing a stick but forgetting that this reduces the value by 5, not 10.

matchstick.title: Intra‑character stick reposition allowed
matchstick.principle: When a single‑stick transformation changes a character’s shape (e.g., V↔X) without adding or removing sticks from other characters, treat it as moving the stick within the same character; only the final character must be a valid numeral/operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a transformation can be achieved by repositioning a stick inside a character rather than moving it between characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick from X to create V but forgetting to keep the other diagonal, leaving an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Numeral‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from one numeral to another, ensure both resulting characters stay valid; a solitary I can be removed entirely (decreasing its value by 1) and the stick can be added to another I to form II (increasing its value by 1).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy can be resolved by transferring a stick between two numerals, especially when one numeral contains a single‑stick I that can be eliminated.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from an I in ‘XVII’ and adding it to the lone I on the left side, but forgetting that the source I disappears, leaving an invalid character.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often removes a stick from a character without checking whether the remaining strokes form a recognized Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every character matches a valid symbol; if a character becomes an unrecognizable shape, discard the move.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may stop after finding a plausible-looking character change and assume the equation is solved.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑compute the integer values of both sides after every candidate move and confirm that the equality holds.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: In the rush to edit characters, the model sometimes deletes a numeral or operator entirely.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Maintain a copy of the original token list and ensure that after a move the token sequence still contains all required parts (numerals, one '=', etc.).

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: Changing ‘+’ to ‘-’ or vice‑versa alters the arithmetic sign, but the model may treat it as a neutral visual change.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Whenever an operator is altered, recompute the expression using the new operator before checking equality.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes adds a new stick or removes a stick without placing it elsewhere, violating the exactly‑one‑stick rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the source and destination of the single stick; ensure exactly one stick is removed and exactly one stick is added.
